svg.title: X3 FPGA board integration
svg.desc: The X3 integrates a CPU/BRAM/debug subsystem, a DDR4 block design, power-up ECC initialization, an ECC register reader and an Ethernet GTY transceiver. The CPU clock is generated by a dedicated GTY transmitter (x3_cpu_clock_gty, channel X0Y29 CPLL) from the shared Ethernet reference clock (or from an MMCM on the differential system clock for CPU_CLK_DIV 3 and 4), with a divide-by-4 clock for UART, loaders and reset timers; the DDR and Ethernet MAC clocks are separate domains, and the system clock divided by two drives the free-running transceiver reset supervisors. Inside frost, the RV64GCBV out-of-order CPU (VLEN 256, Sv39, hardware misaligned-access assist) uses a coherent L1I/L1D/L2 hierarchy and 256 KiB low BRAM with an 8 KiB instruction cache, L0 data reads and write-through stores. SmartConnect (ddr_smc) merges three initiators across clock and width boundaries onto two controller interfaces: S00_AXI carries 512-bit traffic from the FROST cache hierarchy and from x3_ddr_init (which zeroes the 1 GiB region with valid ECC after calibration before releasing CPU, DDR JTAG and ECC reader reset), S01_AXI carries the separate DDR JTAG-AXI burst loader, and S02_AXI (ECC_AXI) carries 32-bit AXI4-Lite polls from x3_ecc_reader. M00_AXI reaches the 512-bit DDR4 memory port and M01_AXI reaches the ECC control registers at region offset 0x40000000 for JTAG and x3_ecc_reader, which reports corrected and uncorrectable errors to the memory error unit in frost. BSCAN USER3 and USER4 share the FPGA TAP with Vivado. Module boxes can span clock domains; only selected connections are shown.

N links the NIC's MAC/PCS to x3_nic_gty; E links x3_ecc_reader to frost's memory error unit.
